records.context: Annotation is the bottleneck in every screen. An extracted image region the model already calls with 0.999 teaches the model nothing when a human labels it; the extracted image regions worth a person's afternoon are the ones sitting on the decision boundary. This module turns an already-scored ``measurements.db`` into a work list ordered so the informative extracted image regions come first.

records.context: **A softmax is not a probability.** Everything here is called an uncertainty *score*, never a confidence. Modern networks are badly calibrated — typically over-confident, and more so the deeper they are (Guo et al., 2017) — so a 0.87 from the head is not "87 % sure". The scores are used for one thing only: putting extracted image regions in an order. Nothing in this module reports a calibrated probability, and neither should anything built on it. See :data:`CALIBRATION_NOTE`.
records.label: spacr.active_learning#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A softmax is not a probability.** Everything here is called an uncertainty *score*, never a confidence. Modern networks are badly calibrated — typically over-confident, and more so the deeper they are (Guo et al., 2017) — so a 0.87 from the head is not "87 % sure". The scores are used for one thing only: putting crops in an order. Nothing in this module reports a calibrated probability, and neither should anything built on it. See :data:`CALIBRATION_NOTE`.
records.translation: **En softmax är ingen sannolikhet.** Allt här kallas en osäkerhets*poäng*, aldrig en konfidens. Moderna nätverk är dåligt kalibrerade — typiskt överkonfidenta, och mer ju djupare de är (Guo et al., 2017) — så 0.87 från huvudet betyder inte "87 % sure". Poängen används till en enda sak: att ordna utklipp. Inget i denna modul rapporterar en kalibrerad sannolikhet, och det bör inte heller något som byggs på den göra. Se :data:`CALIBRATION_NOTE`.

records.context: **Already-annotated extracted image regions never enter the annotation work list.** ``NULL`` in the annotation column is the abstention marker — the extracted image region has not been looked at. ``0`` is a real class, and an annotation work list that re-serves it wastes exactly the resource this module exists to save. The two are distinguished by ``IS NULL``, never by falsiness. (Same convention as :mod:`spacr.agreement`.)
records.label: spacr.active_learning#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Already-annotated crops never enter the queue.** ``NULL`` in the annotation column is the abstention marker — the crop has not been looked at. ``0`` is a real class, and a queue that re-serves it wastes exactly the resource this module exists to save. The two are distinguished by ``IS NULL``, never by falsiness. (Same convention as :mod:`spacr.agreement`.)
records.translation: **Redan annoterade utklipp kommer aldrig in i kön.** ``NULL`` i annoteringskolumnen är markören för avstående — utklippet har inte granskats. ``0`` är en verklig klass, och en kö som serverar det igen slösar exakt den resurs som denna modul finns till för att spara. De två skiljs åt med ``IS NULL``, aldrig genom sanningsvärde. (Samma konvention som :mod:`spacr.agreement`.)

records.context: **The two head shapes are handled separately.** The machine-learning classification model head emits either a single logit (binary; needs a sigmoid) or C logits (multiclass; needs a softmax) — see :func:`spacr.deep_spacr.apply_model_to_tar`. Pushing a single-logit column through a softmax yields a column of 1.0 and destroys the ordering; pushing C logits through a sigmoid can *invert* it. Both are silent failures that produce a confident-looking work list full of nonsense, so :func:`probabilities_from_logits` branches on the shape and the tests pin both directions.
records.label: spacr.active_learning#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The two head shapes are handled separately.** The classifier head emits either a single logit (binary; needs a sigmoid) or C logits (multiclass; needs a softmax) — see :func:`spacr.deep_spacr.apply_model_to_tar`. Pushing a single-logit column through a softmax yields a column of 1.0 and destroys the ordering; pushing C logits through a sigmoid can *invert* it. Both are silent failures that produce a confident-looking queue full of nonsense, so :func:`probabilities_from_logits` branches on the shape and the tests pin both directions.
records.translation: **De två huvudformerna hanteras separat.** Klassificerarhuvudet ger antingen en enda logit (binärt; behöver en sigmoid) eller C logits (flerklass; behöver en softmax) — se :func:`spacr.deep_spacr.apply_model_to_tar`. Att skicka en kolumn med en enda logit genom en softmax ger en kolumn med 1.0 och förstör ordningen; att skicka C logits genom en sigmoid kan *vända* den. Båda är tysta fel som ger en kö som ser säker ut men är full av nonsens, så :func:`probabilities_from_logits` förgrenar sig på formen och testerna låser båda riktningarna.

records.context: ``margin`` and ``least_confidence`` are the same ranking on two classes. For C = 2, ``1 − (p₁ − p₂) = 2·min(p, 1−p) = 2·(1 − max p)``: a linear transform, so identical order and identical ties. They are not two independent choices on a binary screen — they differ only from three classes up, where ``margin`` looks at the top *two* classes while ``least_confidence`` looks only at the top one and ``entropy`` looks at the whole distribution.
records.label: spacr.active_learning#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``margin`` and ``least_confidence`` are the same ranking on two classes. For C = 2, ``1 − (p₁ − p₂) = 2·min(p, 1−p) = 2·(1 − max p)``: a linear transform, so identical order and identical ties. They are not two independent choices on a binary screen — they differ only from three classes up, where ``margin`` looks at the top *two* classes while ``least_confidence`` looks only at the top one and ``entropy`` looks at the whole distribution.
records.translation: ``margin`` och ``least_confidence`` ger samma rangordning för två klasser. För C = 2 gäller ``1 − (p₁ − p₂) = 2·min(p, 1−p) = 2·(1 − max p)``: en linjär transformation, så identisk ordning och identiska oavgjorda fall. De är inte två oberoende val i en binär screen — de skiljer sig först från tre klasser och uppåt, där ``margin`` ser på de *två* högsta klasserna medan ``least_confidence`` bara ser på den högsta och ``entropy`` ser på hela fördelningen.

records.context: The measures above see one model's opinion and call a 50/50 output "uncertain" whether the model is genuinely torn or merely mis-calibrated. records.translation: Måtten ovan ser en enda modells åsikt och kallar en 50/50-utdata "uncertain" oavsett om modellen verkligen är kluven eller bara felkalibrerad. records.translation: 1. anpassar en modell på varje etikett i ``annotation_column``; 2. poängsätter den på en **grupperad** undanhållen uppdelning, så att talet inte är en artefakt av att 190 etiketter kommer från en brunn; 3. skriver tillbaka sannolikheter per klass i ``png_list`` som :data:`ROUND_PRED_PREFIX`-kolumner, vilka :func:`build_queue` föredrar framför den äldre ``pred`` — så att nästa kö verkligen rangordnas om; 4. registrerar rundan, vilket ger :func:`learning_curve` ytterligare en punkt; 5. returnerar :class:`StoppingVerdict` för kurvan hittills.

records.label: spacr.active_learning.should_stop#2

records.source: Why this rule and not another:
records.translation: Varför denna regel och inte en annan:

records.context: **Labels, not rounds, are the unit of cost.** A round is whatever size the annotator felt like; "no improvement for 3 rounds" says nothing when the rounds were 5, 300 and 8 labels. The thing being spent is human attention, one extracted image region at a time, so the window is measured in extracted image regions.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.should_stop#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Labels, not rounds, are the unit of cost.** A round is whatever size the annotator felt like; "no improvement for 3 rounds" says nothing when the rounds were 5, 300 and 8 labels. The thing being spent is human attention, one crop at a time, so the window is measured in crops.
records.translation: **Etiketter, inte rundor, är kostnadsenheten.** En runda har den storlek som annoteraren kände för; "no improvement for 3 rounds" säger ingenting när rundorna var 5, 300 och 8 etiketter. Det som förbrukas är mänsklig uppmärksamhet, ett utklipp i taget, så fönstret mäts i utklipp.

records.context: **It looks *back over* rounds, not *at* the last one.** A single round that happened to land flat is noise; the question is whether the last fifty labels — however they were divided up — bought anything.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.should_stop#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **It looks *back over* rounds, not *at* the last one.** A single round that happened to land flat is noise; the question is whether the last fifty labels — however they were divided up — bought anything.
records.translation: **Den ser *tillbaka över* rundor, inte *på* den senaste.** En enskild runda som råkade bli platt är brus; frågan är om de senaste femtio etiketterna — hur de än fördelades — gav något.

records.context: **It refuses to answer early.** Below ``label_window`` labels since the first recorded round there is no window to measure, and a rule that fired anyway would tell people to stop after their first twelve labels.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.should_stop#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **It refuses to answer early.** Below ``label_window`` labels since the first recorded round there is no window to measure, and a rule that fired anyway would tell people to stop after their first twelve labels.
records.translation: **Den vägrar svara för tidigt.** Under ``label_window`` etiketter sedan den första registrerade rundan finns inget fönster att mäta, och en regel som ändå slog till skulle säga åt folk att sluta efter sina första tolv etiketter.

records.context: **It distinguishes "flat" from "unmeasurable".** Held-out accuracy on 80 objects has a standard error near 0.05; a 0.3 % change is inside the noise, and :attr:`StoppingVerdict.confident` says so instead of dressing it up. Flat *is* still the recommendation — if more labels are not moving a number you can measure, they are not buying anything you can demonstrate — but the reason says the held-out set is too small to prove convergence, which is a different piece of work.
records.label: spacr.active_learning.should_stop#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **It distinguishes "flat" from "unmeasurable".** Held-out accuracy on 80 objects has a standard error near 0.05; a 0.3 % change is inside the noise, and :attr:`StoppingVerdict.confident` says so instead of dressing it up. Flat *is* still the recommendation — if more labels are not moving a number you can measure, they are not buying anything you can demonstrate — but the reason says the held-out set is too small to prove convergence, which is a different piece of work.
records.translation: **Den skiljer "flat" från "unmeasurable".** Undanhållen noggrannhet på 80 objekt har ett standardfel nära 0.05; en förändring på 0.3 % ligger inom bruset, och :attr:`StoppingVerdict.confident` säger det i stället för att försköna det. Platt *är* fortfarande rekommendationen — om fler etiketter inte flyttar ett tal som du kan mäta, ger de inget som du kan påvisa — men skälet anger att den undanhållna uppsättningen är för liten för att bevisa konvergens, vilket är ett annat arbete.

records.context: **A falling curve stops too, and says so.** Accuracy going down is not convergence; it usually means the newest labels disagree with the earlier ones, or that the held-out split moved. Either way, more of the same is the wrong next move.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A falling curve stops too, and says so.** Accuracy going down is not convergence; it usually means the newest labels disagree with the earlier ones, or that the held-out split moved. Either way, more of the same is the wrong next move.
records.translation: **En fallande kurva stoppar också, och säger det.** Sjunkande noggrannhet är inte konvergens; det betyder oftast att de nyaste etiketterna inte stämmer med de tidigare, eller att den undanhållna uppdelningen har flyttats. I båda fallen är mer av samma sak fel nästa steg.

records.context: Selection proceeds in three stages:
records.label: spacr.cell_montage#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Selection proceeds in three stages:
records.translation: Urvalet sker i tre steg:

records.context: 1. :func:`wells_for_coefficient` identifies microplate sample positions with a non-zero fraction of the guide or gene. Gene-level selection sums guide fractions by default; :func:`select_montage_per_guide` evaluates guides separately. 2. :func:`score_window` defines ``target = baseline + effect`` and retains objects within ``half_widths`` robust scales of the target, ordered by ``|score - target|``. The baseline and scale are calculated across the supplied object population rather than separately for each gene. 3. :func:`objects_to_show` selects ``round(n_objects_in_well * guide_fraction_in_well)`` objects from each microplate sample position. Zero-contribution microplate sample positions remain in the plan for reporting.
records.label: spacr.cell_montage#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. :func:`wells_for_coefficient` identifies wells with a non-zero fraction of the guide or gene. Gene-level selection sums guide fractions by default; :func:`select_montage_per_guide` evaluates guides separately. 2. :func:`score_window` defines ``target = baseline + effect`` and retains objects within ``half_widths`` robust scales of the target, ordered by ``|score - target|``. The baseline and scale are calculated across the supplied object population rather than separately for each gene. 3. :func:`objects_to_show` selects ``round(n_objects_in_well * guide_fraction_in_well)`` objects from each well. Zero-contribution wells remain in the plan for reporting.
records.translation: 1. :func:`wells_for_coefficient` identifierar brunnar med en andel av guiden eller genen som inte är noll. Urval på gennivå summerar som standard guideandelarna; :func:`select_montage_per_guide` utvärderar guider separat. 2. :func:`score_window` definierar ``target = baseline + effect`` och behåller objekt inom ``half_widths`` robusta skalor från målet, ordnade efter ``|score - target|``. Baslinjen och skalan beräknas över hela den tillhandahållna objektpopulationen i stället för separat för varje gen. 3. :func:`objects_to_show` väljer ``round(n_objects_in_well * guide_fraction_in_well)`` objekt från varje brunn. Brunnar utan bidrag finns kvar i planen för rapportering.

records.context: Reads ``png_list`` -- which is where :func:`spacr.predictions.merge_cv_predictions` writes the per-object classification score -- and hands it to :func:`spacr.io.crop_rows_from_png_list`, which is the join that recovers ``path_name`` and the integer ``object_label`` a merged extracted image region is cut by. So the frame that comes back serves **both** extracted image region sources: ``png_path`` for :class:`~spacr.crops.PngCropSource`, ``path_name`` plus ``object_label`` for :class:`~spacr.crops.MergedCropSource`.

records.source: Reads ``png_list`` -- which is where :func:`spacr.predictions.merge_cv_predictions` writes the per-object classification score -- and hands it to :func:`spacr.io.crop_rows_from_png_list`, which is the join that recovers ``path_name`` and the integer ``object_label`` a merged crop is cut by. So the frame that comes back serves **both** crop sources: ``png_path`` for :class:`~spacr.crops.PngCropSource`, ``path_name`` plus ``object_label`` for :class:`~spacr.crops.MergedCropSource`.
records.translation: Läser ``png_list`` -- som är där :func:`spacr.predictions.merge_cv_predictions` skriver klassificeringspoängen per objekt -- och lämnar den till :func:`spacr.io.crop_rows_from_png_list`, vilket är den sammanfogning som återvinner ``path_name`` och den heltaliga ``object_label`` som ett sammanslaget utklipp skärs ut efter. Ramen som kommer tillbaka betjänar därför **båda** utklippskällorna: ``png_path`` för :class:`~spacr.crops.PngCropSource`, ``path_name`` plus ``object_label`` för :class:`~spacr.crops.MergedCropSource`.

records.label: spacr.convert#0
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Format converter / importer — vendor microscopy files into Yokogawa TIFFs.
records.translation: Formatkonverterare / importör — leverantörers mikroskopifiler till Yokogawa-TIFF-filer.

records.context: This module converts vendor image files into a layout spaCR can read. It is **decoupled from the mask workflow**: nothing here imports torch, cellpose or :mod:`spacr.core`, so it can be executed, tested and previewed on a laptop with no GPU and no segmentation settings in sight.
records.label: spacr.convert#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: This module converts vendor image files into a layout spaCR can read. It is **decoupled from the mask pipeline**: nothing here imports torch, cellpose or :mod:`spacr.core`, so it can be run, tested and previewed on a laptop with no GPU and no segmentation settings in sight.
records.translation: Denna modul konverterar leverantörers bildfiler till en struktur som spaCR kan läsa. Den är **frikopplad från maskpipelinen**: inget här importerar torch, cellpose eller :mod:`spacr.core`, så den kan köras, testas och förhandsgranskas på en bärbar dator utan GPU och utan segmenteringsinställningar inom synhåll.

records.context: **Z that is not silently flattened.** ``convert_to_yokogawa`` max-projects unconditionally in three of its four branches (ND2, LIF, and both the 3-D and 4-D TIFF cases), and says so nowhere in its output. Here the default is :data:`Z_KEEP` — every image layer is written with its own ``Z##`` — and choosing to project is an explicit ``z_handling='max'``, announced in the plan and recorded per row in the map file.
records.label: spacr.convert#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Z that is not silently flattened.** ``convert_to_yokogawa`` max-projects unconditionally in three of its four branches (ND2, LIF, and both the 3-D and 4-D TIFF cases), and says so nowhere in its output. Here the default is :data:`Z_KEEP` — every plane is written with its own ``Z##`` — and choosing to project is an explicit ``z_handling='max'``, announced in the plan and recorded per row in the map file.
records.translation: **Z som inte plattas ut i tysthet.** ``convert_to_yokogawa`` gör maxprojektion villkorslöst i tre av sina fyra grenar (ND2, LIF och både 3-D- och 4-D-fallen för TIFF), och nämner det ingenstans i sina utdata. Här är standard :data:`Z_KEEP` — varje plan skrivs med sitt eget ``Z##`` — och att välja projektion är ett uttryckligt ``z_handling='max'``, som meddelas i planen och registreras per rad i kartfilen.

records.translation: Designregler

records.context: **No new required dependencies.** ``nd2reader`` / ``czifile`` / ``readlif`` are probed with :func:`importlib.util.find_spec`; when one is missing the affected files are reported as skipped with the package name and the ``pip install`` line, never as an ImportError traceback.
records.label: spacr.convert#12
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **No new required dependencies.** ``nd2reader`` / ``czifile`` / ``readlif`` are probed with :func:`importlib.util.find_spec`; when one is missing the affected files are reported as skipped with the package name and the ``pip install`` line, never as an ImportError traceback.
records.translation: **Inga nya obligatoriska beroenden.** ``nd2reader`` / ``czifile`` / ``readlif`` undersöks med :func:`importlib.util.find_spec`; när ett saknas rapporteras de berörda filerna som överhoppade med paketnamnet och raden ``pip install``, aldrig som en ImportError-traceback.

records.context: **Never overwrite.** Two sources landing on one target name is a *plan-time error* naming both, not a last-writer-wins at convert time. An output that already exists on disk is skipped and counted, so a repeat execution is a no-op rather than a silent rewrite.
records.label: spacr.convert#13
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Never overwrite.** Two sources landing on one target name is a *plan-time error* naming both, not a last-writer-wins at convert time. An output that already exists on disk is skipped and counted, so a re-run is a no-op rather than a silent rewrite.
records.translation: **Skriv aldrig över.** Två källor som hamnar på samma målnamn är ett *fel vid planeringen* som namnger båda, inte att den sista skrivaren vinner vid konverteringen. En utdatafil som redan finns på disk hoppas över och räknas, så att en omkörning inte gör något i stället för att tyst skriva om.

records.context: **Atomic writes.** Every TIFF is written to a temp file in the destination and :func:`os.replace`\ d into place, so an interrupted run leaves no half-written file that the next run mistakes for done.
records.label: spacr.convert#14
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Atomic writes.** Every TIFF is written to a temp file in the destination and :func:`os.replace`\ d into place, so an interrupted run leaves no half-written file that the next run mistakes for done.
records.translation: **Atomära skrivningar.** Varje TIFF skrivs till en temporär fil i målet och flyttas på plats med :func:`os.replace`, så att en avbruten körning inte lämnar någon halvskriven fil som nästa körning misstar för klar.

records.context: :func:`spacr.io.convert_to_yokogawa` already converts ND2/CZI/LIF/TIFF, and it is still the right tool when you want an in-place rename of a flat folder. It does not provide the three features of this module:

records.source: :func:`spacr.io.convert_to_yokogawa` already converts ND2/CZI/LIF/TIFF, and it is still the right tool when you want an in-place rename of a flat folder. It does not provide the three features of this module:
records.translation: :func:`spacr.io.convert_to_yokogawa` konverterar redan ND2/CZI/LIF/TIFF, och den är fortfarande rätt verktyg när du vill byta namn på plats i en platt mapp. Den tillhandahåller inte de tre funktionerna i denna modul:

records.context: **Preview.** It writes as it walks. There is no point at which you can look at "``run1/wt/fov01_C1.tif`` → ``plate1_A01_…C01.tif``" and say no. :func:`plan` produces that table and writes nothing.

records.source: **Preview.** It writes as it walks. There is no point at which you can look at "``run1/wt/fov01_C1.tif`` → ``plate1_A01_…C01.tif``" and say no. :func:`plan` produces that table and writes nothing.
records.translation: **Förhandsgranskning.** Den skriver medan den går igenom filerna. Det finns ingen tidpunkt då du kan titta på "``run1/wt/fov01_C1.tif`` → ``plate1_A01_…C01.tif``" och säga nej. :func:`plan` producerar den tabellen och skriver ingenting.

records.context: **A map you can read back.** It writes a ``rename_log.csv`` whose columns differ per input format (the LIF and TIFF branches record two columns; the ND2 branch records seven; the CZI branch records nine), and nothing in spaCR ever reads it. :func:`write_map` emits one fixed schema and :func:`read_map` / :func:`populate_db_from_map` read it back, so after a run the original filename for any measurement is one SQL join away.

records.translation: **En karta som du kan läsa tillbaka.** Den skriver en ``rename_log.csv`` vars kolumner skiljer sig per indataformat (grenarna för LIF och TIFF registrerar två kolumner; grenen för ND2 registrerar sju; grenen för CZI registrerar nio), och inget i spaCR läser någonsin den. :func:`write_map` ger ut ett enda fast schema och :func:`read_map` / :func:`populate_db_from_map` läser tillbaka det, så att efter en körning är det ursprungliga filnamnet för varje mätning en enda SQL-sammanfogning bort.

Image Lab stores ``zero_is="white"`` data, so such an image is inverted as ``data_ceiling - raw``; the result then looks like Image Lab's own PDF and TIFF exports (dark objects on a light background). ``zero_is="black"`` data is returned as stored.

records.context: 1. the registry knows it — anything unregistered is never a candidate; 2. its kind is not an **original** (:data:`ORIGINAL_KINDS`): nothing in :mod:`spacr.ports` declares that it produces raw images or sequencing reads, so nothing can make them again; 3. a declared **producing module** exists for its kind, and the module the registry recorded is one of them; 4. that module's **inputs are complete** — every recorded input artifact is still registered and still on disk, and :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` says the module could execute in this project right now; 5. it was written by a processing session that **finished** (``status == "complete"``); 6. what is on disk still **fingerprints to what was registered**, so a folder somebody has since dropped a file into is not prunable; 7. it lives **inside the project**, reached without following a symlink; 8. **every** artifact sharing its path passes all of the above — three kinds live in ``measurements.db``, and deleting the file for one of them destroys the other two; 9. no other registered artifact sits inside it or around it, because the bytes belong to the innermost one and a plan must not under-report what it deletes.
records.label: spacr.data_manager#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. the registry knows it — anything unregistered is never a candidate; 2. its kind is not an **original** (:data:`ORIGINAL_KINDS`): nothing in :mod:`spacr.ports` declares that it produces raw images or sequencing reads, so nothing can make them again; 3. a declared **producing module** exists for its kind, and the module the registry recorded is one of them; 4. that module's **inputs are complete** — every recorded input artifact is still registered and still on disk, and :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` says the module could run in this project right now; 5. it was written by a run that **finished** (``status == "complete"``); 6. what is on disk still **fingerprints to what was registered**, so a folder somebody has since dropped a file into is not prunable; 7. it lives **inside the project**, reached without following a symlink; 8. **every** artifact sharing its path passes all of the above — three kinds live in ``measurements.db``, and deleting the file for one of them destroys the other two; 9. no other registered artifact sits inside it or around it, because the bytes belong to the innermost one and a plan must not under-report what it deletes.
records.translation: 1. registret känner till den — inget oregistrerat är någonsin en kandidat; 2. dess typ är inte ett **original** (:data:`ORIGINAL_KINDS`): inget i :mod:`spacr.ports` deklarerar att det producerar råa bilder eller sekvenseringsläsningar, så inget kan skapa dem igen; 3. en deklarerad **producerande modul** finns för dess typ, och den modul som registret registrerade är en av dem; 4. modulens **indata är fullständiga** — varje registrerad indataartefakt är fortfarande registrerad och finns fortfarande på disk, och :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` säger att modulen skulle kunna köras i detta projekt just nu; 5. den skrevs av en körning som **slutfördes** (``status == "complete"``); 6. det som finns på disk har fortfarande **samma fingeravtryck som det som registrerades**, så att en mapp som någon sedan dess har släppt en fil i inte kan rensas; 7. den ligger **inuti projektet**, nådd utan att följa en symbolisk länk; 8. **varje** artefakt som delar dess sökväg klarar allt ovan — tre typer finns i ``measurements.db``, och att ta bort filen för en av dem förstör de andra två; 9. ingen annan registrerad artefakt ligger inuti den eller runt den, eftersom byten tillhör den innersta och en plan inte får underrapportera vad den tar bort.

records.context: Rule 3 also protects other kinds. ``ports.producers_of`` is empty for ``raw-images`` and ``sequencing-reads``, which is *why* originals are safe — and it is empty today for ``channel-stacks`` too, so ``stack/`` is reported as unregistered bytes and never offered, even though it is one of the largest intermediates. This changes only when a port declares that it produces them.

records.source: Rule 3 also protects other kinds. ``ports.producers_of`` is empty for ``raw-images`` and ``sequencing-reads``, which is *why* originals are safe — and it is empty today for ``channel-stacks`` too, so ``stack/`` is reported as unregistered bytes and never offered, even though it is one of the largest intermediates. This changes only when a port declares that it produces them.
records.translation: Regel 3 skyddar också andra typer. ``ports.producers_of`` är tom för ``raw-images`` och ``sequencing-reads``, vilket är *varför* original är säkra — och den är i dag tom även för ``channel-stacks``, så att ``stack/`` rapporteras som oregistrerade byte och aldrig erbjuds, trots att den är ett av de största mellanresultaten. Detta ändras först när en port deklarerar att den producerar dem.

records.context: Nothing is deleted without a plan.  :func:`plan_prune` returns exactly what would go and how much it frees; :func:`prune` refuses to run unless it is handed :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, a digest over that exact path set and byte total, so a confirmation cannot authorise a deletion other than the one that was shown.

records.source: Nothing is deleted without a plan.  :func:`plan_prune` returns exactly what would go and how much it frees; :func:`prune` refuses to run unless it is handed :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, a digest over that exact path set and byte total, so a confirmation cannot authorise a deletion other than the one that was shown.
records.translation: Inget tas bort utan en plan.  :func:`plan_prune` returnerar exakt vad som skulle försvinna och hur mycket det frigör; :func:`prune` vägrar att köras om den inte får :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, en sammanfattning över exakt den uppsättningen sökvägar och den totala bytemängden, så att en bekräftelse inte kan godkänna någon annan borttagning än den som visades.

records.context: 1. the confirmation must equal :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, a digest over the plan's exact paths and byte total, so a token cannot authorise a deletion other than the one it was shown for; 2. every candidate is re-fingerprinted and must still match the plan. Any difference — a file added, a file changed, the folder gone — aborts the whole call before a single delete; 3. the registry write happens next, inside one transaction, counted and verified (see :func:`_verified_write`). A mismatch rolls it back and raises with **nothing on disk deleted**; 4. only then are the files removed; 5. every path is checked to be gone afterwards.
records.translation: 1. bekräftelsen måste vara lika med :attr:`PrunePlan.token`, en sammanfattning över planens exakta sökvägar och totala bytemängd, så att ett token inte kan godkänna någon annan borttagning än den som det visades för; 2. varje kandidat får nya fingeravtryck och måste fortfarande stämma med planen. Varje skillnad — en tillagd fil, en ändrad fil, mappen borta — avbryter hela anropet före en enda borttagning; 3. skrivningen till registret sker därefter, inom en transaktion, räknad och verifierad (se :func:`_verified_write`). En avvikelse återställer den och utlöser ett undantag med **inget på disk borttaget**; 4. först därefter tas filerna bort; 5. varje sökväg kontrolleras efteråt för att vara borta.

records.context: ``ari`` — **background is excluded.** The Adjusted Rand Index over two raw label images is dominated by background: a 1400x1400 microscope field of view is ~95 % background, both models agree it is background, and those agreed pairs swamp everything else. Two models that disagree about every single object still score about 0.999 (``tests/ test_model_compare.py`` asserts exactly that number on a microscope field of view where the foreground agreement is 0.0).
records.label: spacr.model_compare#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``ari`` — **background is excluded.** The Adjusted Rand Index over two raw label images is dominated by background: a 1400x1400 field is ~95 % background, both models agree it is background, and those agreed pairs swamp everything else. Two models that disagree about every single object still score about 0.999 (``tests/ test_model_compare.py`` asserts exactly that number on a field where the foreground agreement is 0.0).
records.translation: ``ari`` — **bakgrunden utesluts.** Adjusted Rand Index över två råa etikettbilder domineras av bakgrunden: ett synfält på 1400x1400 är ~95 % bakgrund, båda modellerna är överens om att det är bakgrund, och dessa överensstämmande par dränker allt annat. Två modeller som är oense om varje enskilt objekt får ändå omkring 0.999 (``tests/ test_model_compare.py`` säkerställer exakt det talet på ett synfält där förgrundsöverensstämmelsen är 0.0).

records.context: So the index is computed over the **union foreground** — the pixels at least one model assigned to an object — with pixels the *other* model left unassigned treated as unclustered singletons rather than as one big background cluster. With background as a single cluster, a model that misses an entire object still scores 1.0, because "one object plus a background blob" and "one object plus a background blob" are the same partition. As singletons, missing half the objects scores 0.50.
records.label: spacr.model_compare#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: So the index is computed over the **union foreground** — the pixels at least one model assigned to an object — with pixels the *other* model left unassigned treated as unclustered singletons rather than as one big background cluster. With background as a single cluster, a model that misses an entire object still scores 1.0, because "one object plus a background blob" and "one object plus a background blob" are the same partition. As singletons, missing half the objects scores 0.50.
records.translation: Indexet beräknas därför över **unionen av förgrunden** — de pixlar som minst en modell tilldelade ett objekt — där pixlar som den *andra* modellen lämnade otilldelade behandlas som oklustrade singletoner i stället för som ett stort bakgrundskluster. Med bakgrunden som ett enda kluster får en modell som missar ett helt objekt ändå 1.0, eftersom "one object plus a background blob" och "one object plus a background blob" är samma partition. Som singletoner ger en miss av hälften av objekten 0.50.

records.context: Computed in closed form from the object overlap matrix (see :func:`adjusted_rand_index`) rather than by materialising millions of singleton labels; ``tests/test_model_compare.py`` checks it against ``sklearn.metrics.adjusted_rand_score`` on the expanded arrays.

records.context: ARI is a *pixel-pair* index, so it is sensitive to boundaries and it is degenerate when a microscope field of view holds one object (a single cluster has no pair structure to agree about). It is reported next to the object-level numbers for that reason, never alone.

records.source: ARI is a *pixel-pair* index, so it is sensitive to boundaries and it is degenerate when a field holds one object (a single cluster has no pair structure to agree about). It is reported next to the object-level numbers for that reason, never alone.
records.translation: ARI är ett index över *pixelpar*, så det är känsligt för gränser och degenererat när ett synfält innehåller ett enda objekt (ett enda kluster har ingen parstruktur att vara överens om). Det rapporteras därför bredvid talen på objektnivå, aldrig ensamt.

records.context: ``iou_matched_fraction`` and ``mean_matched_iou`` — from an **optimal** assignment, not a greedy one. Matching objects between two segmentations is a bipartite assignment problem; picking each object's best partner double-assigns, and picking greedily in descending IoU can leave a pair stranded that an optimal assignment would have kept. Both failures are reproduced in the tests. :func:`match_objects` thresholds the IoU matrix and then runs :func:`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` over it, which is also what ``cellpose.metrics`` does.
records.label: spacr.model_compare#14
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``iou_matched_fraction`` and ``mean_matched_iou`` — from an **optimal** assignment, not a greedy one. Matching objects between two segmentations is a bipartite assignment problem; picking each object's best partner double-assigns, and picking greedily in descending IoU can leave a pair stranded that an optimal assignment would have kept. Both failures are reproduced in the tests. :func:`match_objects` thresholds the IoU matrix and then runs :func:`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` over it, which is also what ``cellpose.metrics`` does.
records.translation: ``iou_matched_fraction`` och ``mean_matched_iou`` — från en **optimal** tilldelning, inte en girig. Att matcha objekt mellan två segmenteringar är ett bipartit tilldelningsproblem; att välja varje objekts bästa partner ger dubbeltilldelningar, och att välja girigt i fallande IoU kan lämna ett par strandat som en optimal tilldelning skulle ha behållit. Båda felen återskapas i testerna. :func:`match_objects` tröskelsätter IoU-matrisen och kör sedan :func:`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` över den, vilket också är vad ``cellpose.metrics`` gör.

records.context: Above an IoU of 0.5 the assignment is provably unique — two objects cannot both overlap a third by more than half of it — so at the default threshold greedy would in fact get the same answer. The optimal assignment is used anyway because ``iou_threshold`` is a knob, and every value below 0.5 (which is where "roughly the same object" lives) makes greedy wrong.

Den optimala tilldelningen används ändå eftersom ``iou_threshold`` är en justerbar parameter, och varje värde under 0.5 (vilket är där "roughly the same object" finns) gör den giriga metoden fel.

records.context: The index is taken over the pixels at least one mask assigned to an object. Pixels the other mask left unassigned stay in the sample but belong to no cluster (each is its own singleton), so a model that misses an object is penalised for it — with background as one shared cluster it would not be. Pixels neither mask claimed are dropped entirely: they are the agreement that would otherwise be the whole answer.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The index is taken over the pixels at least one mask assigned to an object. Pixels the other mask left unassigned stay in the sample but belong to no cluster (each is its own singleton), so a model that misses an object is penalised for it — with background as one shared cluster it would not be. Pixels neither mask claimed are dropped entirely: they are the agreement that would otherwise be the whole answer.
records.translation: Indexet beräknas över de pixlar som minst en mask tilldelade ett objekt. Pixlar som den andra masken lämnade otilldelade stannar i urvalet men tillhör inget kluster (var och en är sin egen singleton), så att en modell som missar ett objekt bestraffas för det — med bakgrunden som ett gemensamt kluster skulle den inte bli det. Pixlar som ingen av maskerna gjorde anspråk på tas bort helt: de är den överensstämmelse som annars skulle utgöra hela svaret.

records.context: This module is built around two properties of OME-NGFF.
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: This module is built around two properties of OME-NGFF.
records.translation: Denna modul är uppbyggd kring två egenskaper hos OME-NGFF.

records.context: **1. The Spacing is built from the SPACE axes only.** A 5-d ngff image has axes ``(t, c, z, y, x)``: the time axis is in seconds, the image data channel axis has no unit at all, and z/y/x are in micrometers. A single ``Spacing`` over all five would have to answer "what unit is this?" with one string, and whatever it answered would be wrong for three of the axes — a stack whose spacing claims ``"um"`` while one of its axes steps in seconds passes the unit check in ``layers.py`` and is then drawn at the wrong scale. So :attr:`OmeZarrImage.spacing` covers z/y/x, and t and c are reported alongside as :class:`Axis` records through :attr:`OmeZarrImage.other_axes`, :attr:`OmeZarrImage.time_axis` and :attr:`OmeZarrImage.channel_axis`. Nothing is lost; the reader does not treat seconds and micrometers as the same kind of number.
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **1. The Spacing is built from the SPACE axes only.** A 5-D NGFF image has axes ``(t, c, z, y, x)``: the time axis is in seconds, the channel axis has no unit at all, and z/y/x are in micrometers. A single ``Spacing`` over all five would have to answer "what unit is this?" with one string, and whatever it answered would be wrong for three of the axes — a stack whose spacing claims ``"um"`` while one of its axes steps in seconds passes the unit check in ``layers.py`` and is then drawn at the wrong scale. So :attr:`OmeZarrImage.spacing` covers z/y/x, and t and c are reported alongside as :class:`Axis` records through :attr:`OmeZarrImage.other_axes`, :attr:`OmeZarrImage.time_axis` and :attr:`OmeZarrImage.channel_axis`. Nothing is lost; the reader does not treat seconds and micrometers as the same kind of number.
records.translation: **1. Spacing byggs endast från SPACE-axlarna.** En 5-D NGFF-bild har axlarna ``(t, c, z, y, x)``: tidsaxeln är i sekunder, kanalaxeln har ingen enhet alls, och z/y/x är i mikrometer. En enda ``Spacing`` över alla fem skulle behöva besvara "what unit is this?" med en enda sträng, och vad den än svarade skulle vara fel för tre av axlarna — en stack vars avstånd påstår ``"um"`` medan en av dess axlar stegar i sekunder klarar enhetskontrollen i ``layers.py`` och ritas sedan i fel skala. Därför täcker :attr:`OmeZarrImage.spacing` z/y/x, och t och c rapporteras bredvid som :class:`Axis`-poster via :attr:`OmeZarrImage.other_axes`, :attr:`OmeZarrImage.time_axis` och :attr:`OmeZarrImage.channel_axis`. Inget går förlorat; läsaren behandlar inte sekunder och mikrometer som samma slags tal.

records.context: **2. Units are translated through an explicit table, and an unknown one is refused.** :data:`NGFF_UNIT_TO_SPACR` is the mapping, written out. A unit that is not in it throws :class:`OmeZarrError`. It would be one line to default to ``"px"`` instead, and that one line is how a 0.65 µm pixel becomes a 0.65 px pixel and every downstream area comes out wrong by a factor of 10^6 — in a column named ``cell_area`` that still looks plausible. The error distinguishes the two cases that need different fixes: a unit NGFF does not define (the file is wrong), and a legal NGFF unit spaCR has no short token for (convert it, e.g. to ``micrometer``).
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **2. Units are translated through an explicit table, and an unknown one is refused.** :data:`NGFF_UNIT_TO_SPACR` is the mapping, written out. A unit that is not in it raises :class:`OmeZarrError`. It would be one line to default to ``"px"`` instead, and that one line is how a 0.65 µm pixel becomes a 0.65 px pixel and every downstream area comes out wrong by a factor of 10^6 — in a column named ``cell_area`` that still looks plausible. The error distinguishes the two cases that need different fixes: a unit NGFF does not define (the file is wrong), and a legal NGFF unit spaCR has no short token for (convert it, e.g. to ``micrometer``).
records.translation: **2. Enheter översätts via en uttrycklig tabell, och en okänd enhet vägras.** :data:`NGFF_UNIT_TO_SPACR` är avbildningen, utskriven. En enhet som inte finns i den utlöser :class:`OmeZarrError`. Det vore en enda rad att i stället falla tillbaka på ``"px"``, och den enda raden är hur en pixel på 0.65 µm blir en pixel på 0.65 px och varje area längre fram blir fel med en faktor 10^6 — i en kolumn som heter ``cell_area`` och som fortfarande ser rimlig ut. Felet skiljer mellan de två fall som kräver olika åtgärder: en enhet som NGFF inte definierar (filen är fel), och en giltig NGFF-enhet som spaCR inte har något kort token för (konvertera den, t.ex. till ``micrometer``).

records.context: **3. A missing unit means pixels, and is reported.** An NGFF file whose space axes carry no ``unit`` is legal and common — it is what every tool that never knew the pixel size writes. That reads back as ``units="px"`` with :attr:`OmeZarrImage.units_declared` ``False`` and a :meth:`OmeZarrImage.describe` line that says the file declared none. It is never silently upgraded to µm, and ``"px"`` is never written out as a unit string, because NGFF has no pixel unit: writing a px spacing emits axes with no ``unit``, which is the same convention read back.

records.context: The writer builds a pyramid by **2x block mean over the two fastest-varying space axes** (see :func:`write_ome_zarr`). It is a box filter and **not a Gaussian pyramid**: there is no pre-filter beyond the box, so it aliases where a properly filtered pyramid would not. It is chosen anyway because it is separable, exact, dependency-free, and the same ``local_mean`` the rest of the NGFF ecosystem writes — matching what other viewers produce matters more here than a marginally better kernel. Striding (``downsample="stride"``) is offered and is **mandatory for label/mask arrays**: the mean of labels 3 and 5 is 4, an object that does not exist.

Striding (``downsample="stride"``) is offered and is **mandatory for label/mask arrays**: the mean of labels 3 and 5 is 4, an object that does not exist.
records.translation: Skrivaren bygger en pyramid genom **2x blockmedelvärde över de två snabbast varierande rumsaxlarna** (se :func:`write_ome_zarr`). Det är ett boxfilter och **inte en Gaussian-pyramid**: det finns inget förfilter utöver boxen, så det ger vikning där en korrekt filtrerad pyramid inte skulle göra det. Det väljs ändå eftersom det är separerbart, exakt, beroendefritt och samma ``local_mean`` som resten av NGFF-ekosystemet skriver — att stämma med vad andra visare producerar väger tyngre här än en marginellt bättre kärna. Stegning (``downsample="stride"``) erbjuds och är **obligatorisk för etikett-/maskarrayer**: medelvärdet av etiketterna 3 och 5 är 4, ett objekt som inte finns.

records.context: Level *k*'s ``scale`` is level 0's ``scale`` multiplied by the cumulative factor 2^k on each downsampled axis. Leaving it at level 0's value is a common NGFF bug — it renders as a pyramid whose coarse levels are a quarter the size of the fine ones and drift off the top-left corner as you zoom. The ``translation`` moves too, and by a different rule per method: a block mean puts the first output element at the *centre* of the block it averaged, half a level-0 pixel in from the edge, so level *k* is translated by ``scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``; a strided level samples element 0 exactly and is not translated at all. Both are written, and asserted in the tests with the numbers spelled out by hand.

records.context: **Chunked.** The array is stored as a grid of independently compressed blocks, so a 100 GB plate is readable a tile at a time. Metadata queries read no array data: :func:`read_ome_zarr` opens a handful of small JSON files and returns the levels, their shapes, their voxel sizes and their chunk grids without reading any chunk, and :meth:`OmeZarrImage.read` with a ``region=`` decodes only the chunks that region intersects. Every byte of chunk data in the pure-Python path passes through one function, :func:`_read_chunk_bytes`, and ``tests/test_ome_zarr.py`` counts its calls to check that reads are lazy.

records.context: The **chunk codecs** are what need compiled code, so they are what the optional extra provides. This module decodes and encodes chunks compressed with ``zlib``, ``gzip``, ``bz2``, ``lzma`` or stored uncompressed using nothing but the standard library, which is why a spaCR-written OME-Zarr round-trips on a plain ``pip install spacr``. records.context: **The transformations.** Level *k*'s ``scale`` is level 0's multiplied by 2^k on each downsampled axis — writing level 0's scale on every level is a common NGFF bug, and it renders as coarse levels that are a quarter the size of the fine ones and slide off the corner as you zoom. The ``translation`` moves too, and differently per method: a block mean centres its first output element half a level-0 pixel inside the edge, so level *k* gets ``translate_0 + scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``, while a strided level samples element 0 exactly and keeps ``translate_0``.
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr.write_ome_zarr#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The transformations.** Level *k*'s ``scale`` is level 0's multiplied by 2^k on each downsampled axis — writing level 0's scale on every level is a common NGFF bug, and it renders as coarse levels that are a quarter the size of the fine ones and slide off the corner as you zoom. The ``translation`` moves too, and differently per method: a block mean centres its first output element half a level-0 pixel inside the edge, so level *k* gets ``translate_0 + scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``, while a strided level samples element 0 exactly and keeps ``translate_0``.
records.translation: **Transformationerna.** Nivå *k*:s ``scale`` är nivå 0:s multiplicerad med 2^k på varje nedsamplad axel — att skriva nivå 0:s skala på varje nivå är ett vanligt NGFF-fel, och det återges som grova nivåer som är en fjärdedel så stora som de fina och glider iväg från hörnet när du zoomar. ``translation`` flyttas också, och olika per metod: ett blockmedelvärde centrerar sitt första utdataelement en halv pixel på nivå 0 innanför kanten, så att nivå *k* får ``translate_0 + scale_0 * (2^k - 1) / 2``, medan en stegad nivå samplar element 0 exakt och behåller ``translate_0``.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

records.translation: **Delarna.** Standard är 1 längs t och c (en visare ritar en kanal för en tidpunkt), :data:`DEFAULT_TILE` på y och x, och :data:`DEFAULT_Z_CHUNK` på alla andra rumsaxlar — omkring 2 MiB per del för uint16. Ange ``chunks=`` för att åsidosätta.

records.translation: Listan ovan handlar om *trohet* mot R. Dessa två handlar om trohet mot en verklig screen, och båda ändrar den simulerade styrkan, så de är **avstängda som standard**. En simulator vars baslinje förskjuts vid en versionshöjning skulle göra varje styrkesiffra som redan citerats från den felaktig, så att slå på någon av dem är en uttrycklig handling.

records.context: **Sequencing error** (:func:`misassign_reads`, ``sequencing_error_rate=``). Both packages treat the read fraction as an exact record of which genotypes were in a microplate sample position. Substitution errors, index hopping, PCR chimeras and mismatch-tolerant demultiplexing all credit reads to the wrong gene. Simulating it says the direct dilution is small — but that it silently disables the unidentified-gene check, turning genes that were correctly reported as untested into confident non-hits. On the reference design that costs ten times more than the dilution does. See :func:`misassign_reads`.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate#19
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Sequencing error** (:func:`misassign_reads`, ``sequencing_error_rate=``). Both packages treat the read fraction as an exact record of which genotypes were in a well. Substitution errors, index hopping, PCR chimeras and mismatch-tolerant demultiplexing all credit reads to the wrong gene. Simulating it says the direct dilution is small — but that it silently disables the unidentified-gene check, turning genes that were correctly reported as untested into confident non-hits. On the reference design that costs ten times more than the dilution does. See :func:`misassign_reads`.
records.translation: **Sekvenseringsfel** (:func:`misassign_reads`, ``sequencing_error_rate=``). Båda paketen behandlar läsandelen som en exakt registrering av vilka genotyper som fanns i en brunn. Substitutionsfel, indexhopp, PCR-chimärer och demultiplexning som tolererar felmatchningar tillskriver alla läsningar fel gen. Simuleringen visar att den direkta utspädningen är liten — men att den tyst inaktiverar kontrollen av oidentifierade gener, så att gener som korrekt rapporterats som otestade blir säkra icke-träffar. I referensdesignen kostar det tio gånger mer än utspädningen gör. Se :func:`misassign_reads`.

records.context: **Well dropout from too few imaged cells** (:func:`drop_low_cell_wells`, ``min_cells_per_well=``). A well where the microscope found three cells enters the fit as one observation next to a well with four hundred. Its positive fraction can only be 0, 1/3, 2/3 or 1, and its standard error is several times the machine-learning classification model's whole signal gap. The Poisson offset stops it dominating the scale of the fit; it does not stop its read-fraction covariate being paired with noise. Dropping such microplate sample positions is what an analyst does by hand, and it costs microplate sample positions — so which way the trade comes out is a thing to simulate rather than assert.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate#20
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Well dropout from too few imaged cells** (:func:`drop_low_cell_wells`, ``min_cells_per_well=``). A well where the microscope found three cells enters the fit as one observation next to a well with four hundred. Its positive fraction can only be 0, 1/3, 2/3 or 1, and its standard error is several times the classifier's whole signal gap. The Poisson offset stops it dominating the scale of the fit; it does not stop its read-fraction covariate being paired with noise. Dropping such wells is what an analyst does by hand, and it costs wells — so which way the trade comes out is a thing to simulate rather than assert.
records.translation: **Bortfall av brunnar på grund av för få avbildade celler** (:func:`drop_low_cell_wells`, ``min_cells_per_well=``). En brunn där mikroskopet hittade tre celler går in i anpassningen som en observation bredvid en brunn med fyrahundra. Dess positiva andel kan bara vara 0, 1/3, 2/3 eller 1, och dess standardfel är flera gånger klassificerarens hela signalskillnad. Poisson-offseten hindrar den från att dominera anpassningens skala; den hindrar inte att dess kovariat för läsandel paras ihop med brus. Att ta bort sådana brunnar är vad en analytiker gör för hand, och det kostar brunnar — så vilket håll avvägningen faller åt är något att simulera snarare än att påstå.

records.context: That product is used as a Bernoulli probability. R's ``rbinom`` returns ``NA`` for ``prob > 1`` with a warning, and the ``NA`` propagates into every downstream count. Clipping keeps the run alive, but it means the realised genes-per-microplate sample position is *below* the requested ``well_abundance_factor_mu`` for the affected genes, so the warning carries the clip count and the worst offender.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate.AbundanceClippedWarning#1

records.source: That product is used as a Bernoulli probability. R's ``rbinom`` returns ``NA`` for ``prob > 1`` with a warning, and the ``NA`` propagates into every downstream count. Clipping keeps the run alive, but it means the realised genes-per-well is *below* the requested ``well_abundance_factor_mu`` for the affected genes, so the warning carries the clip count and the worst offender.
records.translation: Den produkten används som en Bernoulli-sannolikhet. R:s ``rbinom`` returnerar ``NA`` för ``prob > 1`` med en varning, och ``NA`` propagerar in i varje efterföljande antal. Klippningen håller körningen vid liv, men den innebär att det realiserade antalet gener per brunn ligger *under* det begärda ``well_abundance_factor_mu`` för de berörda generna, så varningen bär antalet klippningar och den värsta avvikaren.

records.context: The requested (mean, variance) pair is not attainable by the distribution.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate.ImpossibleMomentsError#0
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The requested (mean, variance) pair is not attainable by the distribution.
records.translation: Det begärda paret (medelvärde, varians) är inte uppnåeligt för fördelningen.

records.context: Raised instead of clamping. A beta distribution cannot have variance above ``mean * (1 - mean)``, and a negative binomial cannot have variance below its mean; quietly moving the request onto the nearest feasible point would hand back samples from a distribution the caller did not ask for, without telling the caller, and the statistical detection sensitivity estimate would then describe a different design from the one requested.

records.translation: Utlöses i stället för att begränsas. En betafördelning kan inte ha en varians över ``mean * (1 - mean)``, och en negativ binomialfördelning kan inte ha en varians under sitt medelvärde; att tyst flytta begäran till närmaste möjliga punkt skulle lämna tillbaka urval från en fördelning som anroparen inte bad om, utan att tala om det för anroparen, och styrkeskattningen skulle då beskriva en annan design än den begärda.

records.context: Mis-assignment gives a gene phantom reads in microplate sample positions it never entered, so the covariate the model regresses positive counts on is a shrunk-toward-uniform version of the truth. The obvious consequence is regression dilution — an attenuated coefficient and a smaller apparent effect — and measuring it in this simulator says that at realistic rates it is **small**: on the 452-gene reference design, 0.5 % mis-assignment moves the hit/non-hit separation from 0.799 to 0.794 among the genes that were identifiable to begin with. records.translation: Felaktig tilldelning ger en gen fantomläsningar i brunnar som den aldrig kom in i, så att kovariaten som modellen regresserar positiva antal på är en mot likformighet krympt version av sanningen. Den uppenbara följden är regressionsutspädning — en dämpad koefficient och en mindre skenbar effekt — och mätningar i denna simulator visar att den vid realistiska frekvenser är **liten**: i referensdesignen med 452 gener flyttar 0.5 % felaktig tilldelning separationen mellan träff och icke-träff från 0.799 till 0.794 bland de gener som var identifierbara från början. Djup sekvensering medelvärdesbildar bort det mesta.

records.context: The consequence that is *not* obvious, and is much larger, is what it does to the genes that were never testable. A gene that landed in every microplate sample position, or in none, has a constant read-fraction column; its coefficient is confounded with the intercept and ``power_model.prepare_model_data`` reports it as unidentified rather than as a non-hit. That check is what keeps a thin design from reporting untestable genes as negative results, and mis-assignment defeats it, because phantom reads give every gene a covariate that *varies*. On the same reference design, 0.5 % error takes the scored library from 317 genes to all 452: the 135 genes that were correctly flagged "untested" become scored non-hits with a covariate made entirely of noise, and the screening experiment-wide separation falls from 0.799 to 0.723 — fourteen times the direct dilution, and all of it from a safeguard being switched off rather than from any loss of signal.

records.context: If ``var <= mean``. The negative binomial is over-dispersed by construction: at ``var == mean`` the size parameter is ``+inf`` (the Poisson limit, which numpy cannot sample as an NB), and below it the size is negative. R's ``assertthat`` allows ``var == mean`` and then hands ``Inf`` to ``rnbinom``, which returns ``NA`` — a whole column of silently missing counts. Use :func:`sample_count_mean_variance` if you want the equi- and under-dispersed cases handled for you.

records.context: ``gene_abundance_alpha`` controls how *even* the library is, and it runs the opposite way from intuition: large alpha gives every gene about ``1/n`` of the pool, alpha near zero concentrates the whole pool on one gene, and ``alpha = 1`` corresponds to a Gini index of 0.5. The real *T. gondii* screening experiment this simulator was fitted to came out at ``alpha = 0.6``, i.e. quite skewed — which is why some genes in it never reached enough microplate sample positions to be callable at all.

records.source: ``gene_abundance_alpha`` controls how *even* the library is, and it runs the opposite way from intuition: large alpha gives every gene about ``1/n`` of the pool, alpha near zero concentrates the whole pool on one gene, and ``alpha = 1`` corresponds to a Gini index of 0.5. The real *T. gondii* screen this simulator was fitted to came out at ``alpha = 0.6``, i.e. quite skewed — which is why some genes in it never reached enough wells to be callable at all.
records.translation: ``gene_abundance_alpha`` styr hur *jämnt* biblioteket är, och det går åt motsatt håll mot intuitionen: ett stort alpha ger varje gen ungefär ``1/n`` av poolen, alpha nära noll koncentrerar hela poolen till en gen, och ``alpha = 1`` motsvarar ett Gini-index på 0.5. Den verkliga *T. gondii*-screen som denna simulator anpassades till hamnade på ``alpha = 0.6``, dvs. ganska skev — vilket är varför vissa gener i den aldrig nådde tillräckligt många brunnar för att alls kunna bedömas.

records.context: Both imaging and sequencing plates originate from *one shared source*: the spot plate. Thus the genotypes in a well are one physical fact observed twice. Each stage uses an independent random stream. Changing the imaging-cell count therefore leaves sequencing draws unchanged. This separation allows meaningful comparison across a sweep of parameter values. Otherwise each point would also contain unrelated randomization.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate.simulate_screen#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The imaging and sequencing plates are both simulated from the *same* spot plate — which genotypes are in a well is one physical fact, observed twice. Each stage draws from its own spawned child stream, so changing the number of imaging cells does not shift the sequencing draws; that independence is what makes a parameter sweep interpretable, since otherwise every point on the sweep would differ by an unrelated re-randomisation as well as by the parameter.
records.translation: Avbildnings- och sekvenseringsplattorna simuleras båda från *samma* spotplatta — vilka genotyper som finns i en brunn är ett fysiskt faktum, observerat två gånger. Varje steg drar från sin egen avknoppade underström, så att en ändring av antalet avbildade celler inte förskjuter sekvenseringsdragningarna; det oberoendet är det som gör ett parametersvep tolkbart, eftersom varje punkt i svepet annars skulle skilja sig genom en orelaterad omslumpning utöver parametern.

records.context: 1. Cells contributing DNA: ``gene_in_well * Count(lambda, var)``. This is normally far larger than the *imaged* count, because sequencing sees the whole well and the microscope sees a few microscope fields of view. 2. Amplification: one lognormal PCR factor per well, ``pcr_factor ~ LogNormal(meanlog=pcr_factor_mu, sdlog=sqrt(pcr_factor_var))``. Note both parameters are on the **log** scale despite their names; a ``pcr_factor_mu`` of 2.0 is a median amplification of ``exp(2) ~ 7.4``. The factor is per well, not per gene, because a well is one PCR reaction — which is exactly why read counts within a well are not independent. 3. Sequencing: reads are drawn from the amplified barcode pool **without replacement** (multivariate hypergeometric), because a finite flow cell reading a finite library is sampling without replacement, and modelling it as multinomial overstates how much independent information deep microplate sample positions carry. 4. **Mis-assignment**, when ``sequencing_error_rate > 0``: a fraction of the reads is credited to the wrong gene. Off by default, because it is not in the R and a silently different baseline would make every number already quoted from this module wrong. See :func:`misassign_reads` for what it models and why it always costs power.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate.simulate_sequencing_plate#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. Cells contributing DNA: ``gene_in_well * Count(lambda, var)``. This is normally far larger than the *imaged* count, because sequencing sees the whole well and the microscope sees a few fields. 2. Amplification: one lognormal PCR factor per well, ``pcr_factor ~ LogNormal(meanlog=pcr_factor_mu, sdlog=sqrt(pcr_factor_var))``. Note both parameters are on the **log** scale despite their names; a ``pcr_factor_mu`` of 2.0 is a median amplification of ``exp(2) ~ 7.4``. The factor is per well, not per gene, because a well is one PCR reaction — which is exactly why read counts within a well are not independent. 3. Sequencing: reads are drawn from the amplified barcode pool **without replacement** (multivariate hypergeometric), because a finite flow cell reading a finite library is sampling without replacement, and modelling it as multinomial overstates how much independent information deep wells carry. 4. **Mis-assignment**, when ``sequencing_error_rate > 0``: a fraction of the reads is credited to the wrong gene. Off by default, because it is not in the R and a silently different baseline would make every number already quoted from this module wrong. See :func:`misassign_reads` for what it models and why it always costs power.
records.translation: 1. Celler som bidrar med DNA: ``gene_in_well * Count(lambda, var)``. Detta är normalt mycket större än det *avbildade* antalet, eftersom sekvenseringen ser hela brunnen och mikroskopet ser några få synfält. 2. Amplifiering: en lognormal PCR-faktor per brunn, ``pcr_factor ~ LogNormal(meanlog=pcr_factor_mu, sdlog=sqrt(pcr_factor_var))``. Observera att båda parametrarna ligger på **log**-skala trots sina namn; ett ``pcr_factor_mu`` på 2.0 är en medianamplifiering på ``exp(2) ~ 7.4``. Faktorn gäller per brunn, inte per gen, eftersom en brunn är en enda PCR-reaktion — vilket är exakt varför läsantal inom en brunn inte är oberoende. 3. Sekvensering: läsningar dras från den amplifierade streckkodspoolen **utan återläggning** (multivariat hypergeometrisk), eftersom en ändlig flödescell som läser ett ändligt bibliotek är ett urval utan återläggning, och att modellera det som multinomialt överskattar hur mycket oberoende information djupa brunnar bär. 4. **Felaktig tilldelning**, när ``sequencing_error_rate > 0``: en andel av läsningarna tillskrivs fel gen. Avstängt som standard, eftersom det inte finns i R och en tyst annorlunda baslinje skulle göra varje tal som redan citerats från denna modul felaktigt. Se :func:`misassign_reads` för vad det modellerar och varför det alltid kostar styrka.

records.source: ``well_abundance_factor_mu`` is the knob that trades genes-per-well against wells-per-gene, and it is the sweep the R package cared most about: with 452 genes, ``mu = 4.6`` gives roughly 4.6 genes per well.
records.translation: ``well_abundance_factor_mu`` är den parameter som väger gener per brunn mot brunnar per gen, och det är det svep som R-paketet brydde sig mest om: med 452 gener ger ``mu = 4.6`` ungefär 4.6 gener per brunn.

records.context: **Probabilities above 1 are clipped, with a warning.** The Bernoulli probability is a product of two independently drawn quantities and nothing constrains it to ``[0, 1]``; at ``alpha = 0.6`` the most abundant gene's share times a ``mu = 4.6`` microplate sample position factor exceeds 1 routinely. R's ``rbinom`` returns ``NA`` there and carries on. This clips to 1 and emits one :class:`AbundanceClippedWarning` carrying the number of clipped cells and the largest offending probability, because a clipped run has a realised genes-per-microplate sample position *below* the one that was requested — the answer is still usable, but not for the parameter value written on it.
records.label: spacr.power_simulate.simulate_spot_plate#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Probabilities above 1 are clipped, with a warning.** The Bernoulli probability is a product of two independently drawn quantities and nothing constrains it to ``[0, 1]``; at ``alpha = 0.6`` the most abundant gene's share times a ``mu = 4.6`` well factor exceeds 1 routinely. R's ``rbinom`` returns ``NA`` there and carries on. This clips to 1 and emits one :class:`AbundanceClippedWarning` carrying the number of clipped cells and the largest offending probability, because a clipped run has a realised genes-per-well *below* the one that was requested — the answer is still usable, but not for the parameter value written on it.
records.translation: **Sannolikheter över 1 klipps, med en varning.** Bernoulli-sannolikheten är en produkt av två oberoende dragna storheter och inget begränsar den till ``[0, 1]``; vid ``alpha = 0.6`` överstiger den rikligaste genens andel gånger en brunnsfaktor på ``mu = 4.6`` rutinmässigt 1. R:s ``rbinom`` returnerar ``NA`` där och fortsätter. Detta klipper till 1 och ger ut en enda :class:`AbundanceClippedWarning` som bär antalet klippta celler och den största felaktiga sannolikheten, eftersom en klippt körning har ett realiserat antal gener per brunn *under* det som begärdes — svaret är fortfarande användbart, men inte för det parametervärde som står på det.
